faqs.q: How do I solarize a photo?

faqs.a: Threshold 128 inverts the brighter half of tones — the classic look. Lower thresholds invert more of the image; higher thresholds invert only the brightest highlights.

It is inspired by the Sabattier effect from film photography, where partially developed prints were re-exposed to light. The digital version inverts tones above a threshold for a similar surreal feel.

solarize-effect.formula:
for each channel v:

keyFacts: Solarization inverts every channel value above your threshold (v → 255 − v).
Values at or below the threshold are left completely untouched.
A mid threshold of 128 inverts roughly the brighter half of the image.
Threshold 0 inverts almost everything; threshold 255 inverts nothing.
The preview updates live as you drag the slider.

limitations: Solarization is a stylistic effect — results are surreal by design, not natural.
The threshold applies equally to all three channels; per-channel control is not included.
Very dark photos show almost no change until the threshold drops very low.
Animated GIFs are processed as a single still frame.

solarize-effect.workedExample:
Threshold 128 on two channel values:
value 200 > 128 → 255 − 200 = 55 (inverted)
value 100 ≤ 128 → stays 100 (untouched)
So a bright sky pixel (210, 220, 230) becomes the dark surreal (45, 35, 25), while shadow pixels below 128 keep their natural color.
